summary:
No Ulsan-specific ordinance, directive, enforcement practice or documented incident concerning transgender people was identified in the available sources. The city stands under the national framework of South Korea, and the assessment of that framework belongs to the national record rather than to this one.

Two national rulings bind in Ulsan because they are final and generally applicable: the appellate decision finalising a 300,000 won damages award against the state over police advice that a transitioning person avoid women's public restrooms, and the May 2024 regional court decision removing sex-reassignment surgery as a prerequisite for changing registered sex. Neither case arose in Ulsan, and no local dispute, charge or facility dispute involving a transgender visitor or resident appears in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The evidence that reaches Ulsan is imported rather than generated locally. The restroom judgment came through the Seoul appellate courts, the surgery-prerequisite ruling through a regional court in Yeongdong, and the supporting survey and damages figures cited alongside them through the National Human Rights Commission of Korea and a Daegu District Court bench sitting in Pohang. Ulsan therefore has no documented record of its own on these questions, and nothing in the sources supports ranking the city's practice above or below other South Korean jurisdictions.

The absence of local incidents should not be read as absence of exposure. Where no local case exists, the practical position of a trans visitor in Ulsan is set by how national courts and national agencies have applied the rules elsewhere, and by the general documented pattern of street and institutional hostility recorded at the national level.
localsOnly:
Residents of Ulsan have access to the same judicially enforced restroom right and the same route to changing registered sex without surgery as elsewhere in South Korea, since both rulings bind territorially. No Ulsan Metropolitan City ordinance, city hall directive, municipal service arrangement or local anti-discrimination mechanism specific to gender identity was found in the sources, so resident protections rest on national statutes and national court practice alone.

No local institution in Ulsan, whether a hospital, school board or city facility operator, is documented either as accommodating or as refusing transgender residents. Local practice on restroom designation, school facilities and hospital admission for transgender patients is simply not recorded.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Ulsan Metropolitan City has issued its own guidance on restroom access, facility designation, hospital admission of transgender patients or reporting of hate incidents is unresolved; the available sources are national press reports and do not address the city's administration.

The supporting figures attached to the restroom findings, including a 2021 National Human Rights Commission of Korea survey of 591 transgender respondents and a 2021 Daegu District Court award of 7 million won against a beauty academy, were generated outside Ulsan and are not verified here for the city. Local enforcement statistics for Ulsan, and any police or municipal practice specific to the city, remain not sourced.
